name: Thick-Grip Deadlift / Fat Bar Deadlift
description: The thick-grip deadlift is performed with a barbell that has a diameter much larger than a standard bar (typically 50-65mm vs 28mm), or with thick grip sleeves applied to a standard bar. The larger diameter prevents the fingers from wrapping fully around the bar, dramatically increasing grip strength demand. The movement itself is identical to a standard deadlift, but grip becomes the primary limiting factor rather than leg or back strength.

execution.starting_position: Approach the thick-bar deadlift set up at floor height. Stand with feet hip-width, bar over mid-foot. Grip the bar double overhand — no hook grip, no straps.
execution.setup_instructions: Fat bar or axle is preferred. Alternatively use thick grip sleeves on a standard bar. No chalk removal — the thick grip is intentional.
steps: Step 1: Set up as a conventional deadlift — hinge at the hips, flat back, lats tight.
Step 2: Grip the thick bar as hard as possible — it will not feel fully locked.
Step 3: Drive the floor away, maintaining back position, until standing erect.
Step 4: Lower the bar under control back to the floor.
execution.breathing_instructions: Deep breath and brace before the pull, exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Using standard bar with straps (negates the grip demand)
safety_considerations: The thick bar will slip more easily than standard — maintain maximum grip tension throughout
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Floor to full hip and knee lockout.
coaching_cues: Grip is the point — squeeze everything
Same cues as a standard deadlift
